answer: Under correlated-attribute scramble admission, each applicant to the ledge network presents a hardware-attested entropy fingerprint hashed into a shared k-decision list, and a batch admits at most the distinct physical devices proven, say 8. A farmer with one enclave minting 1,000 agents needs 125 batches, so cost jumps from $5 to $625 in scarce secure-device hours. An honest cedar volunteer pays $5 once for one device, while the nadir of attacker yield is one identity per real chip, making mass forgery economically pointless for any coordinated adversary.
